description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian dish known for its rich, creamy tomato gravy and tender chicken. This classic recipe delivers an authentic restaurant-style experience right in your home. Its irresistible flavors make it a perfect choice for any special occasion or a comforting weeknight meal.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt another 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, whole green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, soaked cashews, and 1/2 cup water or chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-12 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamoms if desired, though they can be blended in.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, you may pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is optional but recommended for a restaurant-style finish.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, sugar, and crushed kasoori methi. Stir well and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the gravy. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and the heavy cream. Cook for 1-2 minutes, just until heated through, do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Garnish with a drizzle of extra heavy cream and fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with basmati rice, naan bread, or roti.

tips: For best results, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be.
Do not skip soaking the cashews; it helps achieve a truly creamy and smooth gravy texture without needing too much cream.
Always add heavy cream at the very end and avoid boiling the gravy after its addition, as it can curdle. Just heat it gently until warm.
article:
## Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: Your Guide to Authentic Indian Flavors

Indian cuisine is a symphony of aromas, textures, and tastes, and few dishes capture its essence quite like the universally adored Butter Chicken. Known in its native tongue as Murgh Makhani, this iconic dish has captivated palates worldwide with its rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato gravy enveloping tender pieces of chicken. It’s a dish that evokes comfort, celebration, and the warmth of home-cooked goodness. While often enjoyed in bustling Indian restaurants, the true magic lies in preparing it yourself, allowing the intoxicating fragrance of simmering spices and butter to fill your kitchen. This comprehensive guide will walk you through the journey of creating your own authentic Butter Chicken at home, transforming simple ingredients into an unforgettable culinary masterpiece.

## What is Classic Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

The story of classic Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, begins in the bustling lanes of Delhi, India, in the 1950s. It was at the Moti Mahal restaurant, a culinary landmark, that this dish was first conceived. Legend has it that the chefs, needing to utilize leftover tandoori chicken, simmered it in a rich, tomato-based gravy laden with butter and cream. The result was a revelation – a dish so exquisitely balanced and flavorful that it quickly rose to prominence, becoming a staple of Indian cuisine and a global sensation.

The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly describing its core ingredients. At its heart, it's a dish characterized by succulent pieces of chicken (traditionally tandoor-cooked, though pan-fried or grilled works beautifully at home) swimming in a velvety smooth, subtly sweet, and tangy gravy. This gravy derives its signature flavor from pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala and kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and, of course, generous amounts of butter and fresh cream. Unlike many fiery Indian curries, Butter Chicken is renowned for its mild yet deeply complex flavor profile, making it a favorite among those new to Indian food and seasoned enthusiasts alike.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of fresh ingredients. Here’s what you’ll need:

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

**For the Gravy:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 large onion, roughly chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1-2 green chilies, slit (adjust to your spice preference)
*   800g canned crushed tomatoes, or 4-5 large fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, optional)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder)
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances acidity)
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed between palms
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus extra for garnish
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed

**For Garnish:**
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create your own restaurant-quality Butter Chicken:

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate and the chicken to tenderize.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Heat a tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken for 3-5 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Gravy Base**
In the same pan, melt the remaining butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes and soaked cashews (if using). Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have softened and the mixture has thickened slightly.

**Step 4: Blend the Gravy**
Remove the pan from heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Carefully transfer the contents to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky gravy, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing down to extract all the liquid and discarding any solids. This step is crucial for the signature smooth texture of Butter Chicken.

**Step 5: Finish the Gravy**
Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the red chili powder, garam masala, sugar, kasoori methi, and salt to taste. Stir well and simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the gravy to thicken to your desired consistency. If it's too thick, add a little water or chicken broth.

**Step 6: Combine and Serve**
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, ensuring the chicken is heated through and has absorbed the gravy's flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream. Simmer for just 1-2 minutes more; do not boil after adding cream, as it can curdle.

Garnish generously with fresh cilantro and a swirl of extra cream, if desired. Your homemade Butter Chicken is ready!

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few insider tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight marination truly makes a difference.
*   **Chicken Choice:** Boneless, skinless chicken thighs are often preferred over breasts as they remain juicier and more forgiving during cooking.
*   **Silky Smooth Gravy:** Don't skip blending the gravy base thoroughly. Straining it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending is the secret to achieving that luxurious, velvety texture that defines authentic Murgh Makhani.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) impart a unique, slightly bitter, yet sweet aroma that is absolutely crucial for the authentic flavor of Butter Chicken. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their oils.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust seasonings throughout the cooking process. The sugar helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes, and salt brings out all the flavors. Don't be afraid to tweak it to your preference.
*   **Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream:** These ingredients are fundamental to the richness and "makhani" (buttery) character of the dish.

## Serving Suggestions

A bowl of comforting Butter Chicken deserves equally delightful accompaniments. It pairs perfectly with:

*   **Naan bread:** Warm, fluffy naan is ideal for soaking up every last bit of the luscious gravy.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or aromatic jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast to the richness.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian flatbreads also make excellent dippers.
*   **Side Salad or Raita:** A simple cucumber and onion salad or cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) can cut through the richness.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic recipe is divine, Butter Chicken is also wonderfully adaptable:

*   **Vegetarian Options:** If you love Butter Chicken, but prefer a vegetarian option, you can easily substitute the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) to make Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu, chickpeas, or a medley of mixed vegetables.
*   **Dairy-Free:** For a dairy-free version, use coconut milk or coconut cream instead of heavy cream, and olive oil or a plant-based butter alternative instead of butter. The flavor profile will shift slightly but will still be delicious.
*   **Spicier Kick:** To increase the heat, add more green chilies or a pinch of cayenne pepper along with the red chili powder.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, opting for low-fat cream or a smaller portion. You can also bake or grill the chicken instead of pan-frying to reduce oil.
*   **Smoky Flavor (Dhungar Method):** For an authentic smoky touch, heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot. Place it in a small bowl within the gravy, pour a teaspoon of ghee or oil over it, and quickly cover the pan for a few minutes to infuse a smoky aroma.

Mastering the art of homemade Butter Chicken is a rewarding culinary achievement. This classic Murgh Makhani recipe, with its tender chicken and exquisite creamy gravy, is more than just a meal; it's an experience. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your senses with one of India's most beloved dishes. Enjoy the journey of flavors!
